title: Welcome as home (R7)

bullets: Mode: the welcome tab stops being a Persuade page and becomes an Operate surface: return to work in one step, see which connections are healthy, start a first connection.

Fixture (synthetic, same in every concept): 7 connections across all six 1.0 engines (HSQLDB, H2, SQLite, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL x2) tagged local, development, staging and production, and 6 recent items (tables, a view, a console, a script). The long-list state adds 8 tenant connections and 34 recent items.
MariaDB and SQLite have no type or icon in the plugin yet: they use the generic database icon as a labeled placeholder.

Renders: Swing painting of real IntelliJ components (SearchTextField, InlineBanner, Tree, ActionLink, JButton) at 2x density, FlatLaf approximating the IDE themes, DejaVu Sans 13 standing in for Inter. Font 2.0 doubles the UI font with the IDE scale unchanged.
Font 2.0 findings (all concepts): icons keep their size, as in the IDE where icons follow UI scale and not font size; long hosts truncate; every body scrolls so nothing is lost.

Motion personality (proposed default, owner to confirm): quiet and IDE-native. Feedback 100-150 ms, state changes 150 ms, one authored moment per surface. Ease-out-quart, cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1). Exits about 2/3 of entrances. No bounce.
Instant by design (platform list behavior, no animation): filtering results, moving the selection, expanding and collapsing groups, opening an item.
Reduced motion: drop every movement, keep opacity and color changes that carry meaning. Hook to the IDE's animation settings at build time (which flag to use is still to be checked).
Errors name the problem and the recovery, inline (InlineBanner), never a modal.
Banned in every direction: marketing hero, card grids, colored side bars on rows, color-only status, gray text on tinted surfaces, monospace as decoration, modals for open failures.

concepts.name: 00 Current
concepts.intro: The welcome tab as it ships in 0.2.0-alpha. It has one connection in the returning state, because the production panel only reads the connection list.

Rendered from the production class, unchanged.

concepts.name: 02 Connection board
concepts.thesis: Home is the health of your connections; refuses the 'links page' default.
concepts.intro: One row per connection, with its environment tag, live status and the objects you last opened there. You see at a glance what is reachable and where production is before you open anything.
how: Data: 7 connections, 6 recent items attached to their connection.
Filter field: matches names, hosts and environment tags.
Click a connection: opens it in the explorer. Click an object link: opens that table, console or script.
Unreachable connections show when they were last reached and Retry.
Narrow width: the status moves into the subline so it is never lost.
New connection is the one button; everything else is a link.
states: Every connection with tag, status and last objects. Click an object to reopen it.
Six engines with Connect links. Click one to open the connection dialog for that engine.
Type in the filter; only Staging remains, with the match in bold.
“prod-eu” matches no name, host or tag. Clear filter restores the list.
On open, server connections show Checking… until the ping returns. Local files are known at once.
Opening PUBLIC.ORDERS on Staging failed. The banner names the host and offers Retry and Edit connection.
The list scrolls; the header and filter stay fixed.
Status moves into the subline; the button shortens to New…

concepts.name: 03 Command home
concepts.thesis: Home is one field; refuses the 'page of sections' default.
concepts.intro: A search field with ranked results under it. With an empty field it lists recent items; typing searches recents, tables in schemas Lattice already loaded, and connections. Enter opens the selection.
how: Data: 6 recent items; table matches from the fixture schemas.
Up/Down: move the selection. Enter: open. Alt+Enter: open in a console.
Groups: Recent, Tables in loaded schemas, Connections; matches in bold.
Errors appear under the field, so the field keeps focus.
First run: the field accepts an engine name; results are the six engines.
states: Recent items, first one selected. Press Enter to reopen PUBLIC.CUSTOMERS.
Six engines; type “post” and press Enter to connect to PostgreSQL.
Recent, table and connection matches grouped, best first.
Says what search covers and offers Refresh schemas and New connection.
Recents show at once (local history); table search waits for schemas.
Enter on the Analytics console: the host timed out. Banner under the field: Retry, Edit connection.
Shows 8, says how many more, and asks you to type to narrow.

concepts.name: 04 Explorer home
concepts.thesis: No welcome tab at all; refuses the idea that a plugin owns an editor tab.
concepts.intro: The editor area belongs to your code. Lattice's home moves into its tool window (a Recent section above the connection tree) and into a Lattice tab in Search Everywhere, which you can reach from anywhere with Double Shift.
how: Data: the same 7 connections and 6 recent items; the tree shows the Local development schema expanded.
Tool window: Recent (4 items, collapsible) above the connection tree; status and tags inline in each tree row.
Search Everywhere: Double Shift, then Tab to Lattice; Enter opens, Alt+Enter opens in a console.
First run: the tool window's empty state lists the six engines.
Errors show as a banner at the top of the tool window and in red on the tree row.
states: Recent above the tree. Double-click a table to open it.
Empty tool window with the six engines. Click one to open the connection dialog.
The tree narrows to matching tables with their connection and schema.
Says that only loaded schemas are searched; offers Refresh schemas.
Server rows say Checking… until the ping returns.
Banner at the top, row text in red: Unreachable.
Recent stays at 4 with a More link; the tree scrolls.
Recent context truncates with an ellipsis. Tree rows clip at the edge, cutting tags: the build must shorten tags or move them to the tooltip at this width.
Double Shift, Tab to Lattice, type “ord”. Approximation painted from labels, not the platform popup.

motionRows.title: Focal · first connection arrives in the tree

spec.moves: New tree row rises 8 px and fades in with accent tint; next-step links fade in
spec.ms: 240 rise; tint fades 400 after a 200 hold
spec.reduced: No rise; row appears at once with the tint, tint fades over 400 ms

concepts.limits: The tool window header and toolbar are labels, not the platform ActionToolbar. The Search Everywhere frame is an approximation; a real contributor would use the platform popup. Removing the tab also removes the What's New entry point from it, so What's New would move to a notification.

recommendation: 02 Connection board is best when you have many connections and production safety matters, but it is the longest page and splits recents across connections. 03 Command home is fastest for returning work and holds up best at narrow width, but it depends on the field's prompt to be discoverable and shows connection health only on failure. 04 Explorer home (radical) frees the editor area and works from anywhere through Search Everywhere, but it needs a Search Everywhere contributor and gives up the one large surface for first-run guidance. Pick: 04, with 03's ranked search as its Search Everywhere tab and 02's environment tags and status inline in the tree. Reason: Lattice is a data tools layer inside the IDE, and the IDE already has a home for tools (tool windows) and for jumping (Search Everywhere); a plugin-owned tab competes with the user's code. Fallback if you want to keep a tab: 03 with 02's status and tags in each result's subline.
